clue.text: Square upright

definitions.meaning: a square person is conventional and honest
upright means erect, not bent or leaning

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday meanings of the word: conventional or honest, and vertical rather than crooked.

clue.text: Associate team with excitement

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a kick is a thrill or buzz of excitement

explanation.surface: A colleague who joins a team for the thrill of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or partner, a junior associate.

clue.text: Pack round inside to secure plant

parts.note: to ram is to pack something down tightly

indicators.note: the round letter goes inside the word meaning to secure

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or secure
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: tamp down the soil round a plant to keep it firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampion is a bellflower grown for its edible roots, a garden plant.

clue.text: Bone used in Algonquin customs

indicators.note: the letters are found used within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A bone carving that features in Native American tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus or anvil is one of the three tiny bones of the middle ear.

clue.text: Dispirited cashier or the banker

indicators.note: to cashier an officer is to break him, so the letters of the following words are broken up

explanation.surface: A bank teller is despondent, or else the banker is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' looks like a bank clerk beside 'banker', but it is the verb: to cashier or break an officer, so it signals that OR THE BANKER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartbroken is crushed with grief, utterly dispirited.

clue.text: Save on small parts

parts.note: to spare is to save or keep back
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Advice to economise by buying smaller components.
explanation.definitionFit: Spares are replacement components kept in reserve, spare parts.

clue.text: One who is naturally religious?

parts.note: read 'naturally' literally: a believer whose faith identifies God with nature itself

explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist holds that God and the natural universe are one, so worship is directed at nature.

clue.text: Artist to stand up with vase

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A painter is made to stand beside a vase, as if for a still life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stand up' reads as one verb phrase, but 'up' is the reversal signal for this down light. Sir Henry Raeburn was a Scottish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Raeburn was a leading Scottish portrait painter, so a well-known artist.

clue.text: Utter shock for Arab leader

indicators.note: utter here is the verb, to speak, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: to shake someone is to shock or upset them

explanation.surface: A complete surprise for a Middle Eastern ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete, but it is the verb to speak: SHAKE spoken gives the usual British pronunciation of the Arabic title.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikh is the chief of an Arab tribe or family, an Arab ruler.

clue.text: Tom cared about being seen as a populist

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tom's concern for ordinary folk wins him a reputation as a man of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A democrat champions rule by ordinary people, as a populist claims to.

clue.text: Appropriate point for extension

parts.note: to annex is to appropriate or seize territory
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Deciding on a suitable spot for a building extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective (suitable) but is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an extension.

clue.text: Odour hanging around jumpers, for instance

indicators.note: hanging around signals the word turning round to run backwards

parts.note: a stink is a bad smell or odour

explanation.surface: A smell clinging to woollen pullovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Knits are knitted garments, of which pullovers are an example.

clue.text: Expression of sympathy from criminal lot?

parts.note: a tough is a thug or hoodlum
one's lot is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: Condolences offered by a gang of crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to commiserate with someone's misfortune, often with little real sympathy.

clue.text: Pose adopted by pin-up Angela Monday lacking allure?

annotationWithheld.clue: Pose adopted by pin-up Angela Monday lacking allure?

clue.text: Not certain son's sorted out alarm

indicators.note: the letters are sorted out into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: Uncertainty that the son has fixed things causes worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is a feeling of dismay and anxiety, synonymous with alarm.

clue.text: Roughly one third added to medium port

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters are handled roughly and rearranged

explanation.surface: An approximate fraction being added to a middling quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Trondheim is a Norwegian city and seaport on a fjord.

clue.text: Pretended to be emotionally upset

definitions.meaning: assumed for show, as an accent can be put on

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: assumed falsely for effect, and stirred or moved in one's feelings.

clue.text: Causes damage to chimneys? Administer a beating

definitions.meaning: read the phrase as ..., striking the chimney pots from a roof
to outclass or thrash an opponent soundly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to beat easily; split differently it describes knocking chimney pots off a roof.

clue.text: Profit from fatality

definitions.meaning: making a big financial gain, as in a stock-market windfall

explanation.definitionFit: Making a big gain and causing a death are both common senses of the word.

clue.text: Awful sofa in yellow tabaret initially 11 February 2002 Registered as a newspaper with the Post Office seen as inferior?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Awful sofa in yellow tabaret initially 11 February 2002 Registered as a newspaper with the Post Office seen as inferior?': masthead text has intruded; wordplay ana(SOFA) + OR (yellow) + T needs the clue without it, and no scan confirms the printed words
annotationWithheld.clue: Awful sofa in yellow tabaret initially 11 February 2002 Registered as a newspaper with the Post Office seen as inferior?

clue.text: Control group

definitions.meaning: a shoal, as of fish or whales

explanation.definitionFit: To train or discipline, and a shoal of fish, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Wrong idea clan gets about old. Scotland

indicators.note: the anagram goes about, or around, the letter for old
something wrong is in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistaken notion about a Highland clan takes hold, in an old Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The full stop after 'old' is an OCR artefact; 'Scotland' is the definition. 'gets about' means the shuffled letters surround the O for old.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin and poetic name for Scotland.

clue.text: Run out of words at this stage?

indicators.note: out of signals one piece being taken out of another

parts.note: a phrase is a group of words
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A speaker finds they have nothing left to say at this point.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase is one stage in a process or development.

clue.text: Suppose one's wearing mail

indicators.note: the post surrounds the letter as clothes surround a wearer

parts.note: post is mail
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Imagining someone dressed in chain mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' suggests armour, but it is the post.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as an assumption, to suppose.

clue.text: Charged to get into alternative musical

indicators.note: the charged word gets into the word for an alternative

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: Someone is charged to get into an alternative show.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Member of plane spotting group?

parts.note: a youth group member whose scouting, or spotting, is linked with aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: Air Scouts are a branch of the Scout movement with an aviation focus.

clue.text: Plant you've to stick in shelter

indicators.note: the stick word is put in the shelter word

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Gardening instruction: put a plant in a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume is a plant of the pea family.

clue.text: Upset when Italian's brought in stone dead

indicators.note: the Italian is brought in to the stone word

parts.note: agate is a semi-precious stone
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed when an Italian is brought in stone dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means troubled and nervous, synonymous with upset.
